reference.title: Effects reference
reference.shortdesc: The built-in effects, what each one does, and the parameters that matter.

section.p: includes several built-in effects. Select a region of audio, then choose an effect from the Effect menu.

messagepanel.consequence: The output can exceed 0 dB and reach your speakers or headphones as a sudden, very loud burst.
messagepanel.howtoavoid: Leave Allow clipping off unless you intend to clip, and preview at low volume.

row.entry: Increases or decreases the volume of the selection.
Removes steady background noise such as hum, hiss or fan noise. Needs a noise profile.
Noise reduction (dB): 6 to 12 for mild noise, 12 to 24 for heavy; sensitivity; frequency smoothing.
Reduces the dynamic range: quiet parts louder, loud parts quieter.
Threshold (dB), ratio (for example 3:1), attack and release times.
Sets the peak amplitude to a target level and optionally removes DC offset.
Peak amplitude (dB), typically -1.0; Remove DC offset.
Ramps the volume of the selection up from silence, or down to it.
None: a linear fade over the selection.
